To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the pH of the reaction medium has a significant effect on the polymerization of the bacterial cytoskeletal protein FtsZ.
the pH dependence of FtsZ polymerisation is a complex function of the nature of the pH-dependent interactions that FtsZ forms with itself and with its associated proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanism of FtsZ polymer formation, and how this relates to the pH dependence of FtsZ activity in vivo.
the fundamental mechanism of FtsZ polymer formation.
the pH-dependent assembly and bundling of FtsZ polymorphic filaments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

FtsZ polymerizes in a GTP-dependent fashion at neutral pH and at lower pHs it polymerizes in a manner that is GTP-dependent but also involves the formation of bundles of protofilaments, which are stabilized by interactions with YgfE and divalent cations.
FtsZ is a very pH sensitive protein, with the GTP hydrolysis rate being pH dependent.
FtsZ polymerizes at pH 6.5, 6 and 7.5, but that the nature of the polymers formed changes with pH.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lowering the pH to pH 6.0 changes the polymerization behaviour of FtsZ from that of protofilaments to protofilaments that bundle together into larger structures.
the FtsZ polymer is pH dependent, with the pH dependence being a function of the pH dependence of the GTP hydrolysis reaction.

lowering the pH of the polymerization medium from 7.0 to 6.8 has the effect of increasing the rate of FtsZ polymer formation, while lowering the pH to below 6.0 stabilizes the protofilaments and inhibits polymerization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pH dependence of FtsZ polymer formation is not simply the pH dependence of the FtsA-FtsZ interaction.
FtsZ is able to form stable protofilaments at low pH and that the protofilaments can associate into bundles, and that these bundles are stabilized by the FtsZ protofilaments themselves.
the pH of the cytosol has a profound impact on the behaviour of FtsZ and thus cell division.
